newsitem.title: USA: Ashland set to sell upstream unit, no IPO.
newsitem.headline: Ashland set to sell upstream unit, no IPO.

text.p: Ashland Inc has abandoned plans to spin off its exploration unit and instead is in talks to sell the business for about $600 million.
Sources familiar with the discussions identified leading buyers as Equitable Resources Inc and privately-held Eastern Group, which is 83 percent-owned by Norway's Statoil.
Ashland, which earlier announced plans to join refining operations with USX-Marathon Group, may vote on the deal at a board meeting later Thursday, the sources said.

Bidding for the Blazer Energy Corp unit, which includes valuable properties in the Appalachian region, intensified over the past few weeks and several companies that had expressed interest dropped out of the race, the sources said.

An Ashland spokesman declined to comment on the potential transaction. The company had filed for an initial public offering of the unit and last month said it was also considering other options, including a sale.
A spokesman for Eastern declined to comment. Equitable Resources could not immediately be reached for comment.
Ashland's decision to sell the exploration business instead of spinning it off was partly fueled by a recent burst of interest in Appalachian properties, sources said.

Financial buyer Texas Pacific Group recently announced a transaction to buy Belden & Blake Corp for $302 million. And independent producer Alamco Inc also has said it is in talks about a possible transaction.

The sources said at least five buyers initially considered Ashland's exploration unit, whose Appalachian properties produced a record 82 million cubic feet per day last year. Other companies that are believed to have expressed interest are Dominion Resources Inc and Consolidated Natural Gas Co.
The sale of the exploration unit, combined with the downstream alliance, will enable Ashland to concentrate on its growing chemicals, Valvoline motor oil and APAC highway paving businesses.
Shares of Ashland were up 1-5/8 at 47-1/8 in early afternoon trade.

The sale of the unit would be the latest move in a reorganization undertaken by Ashland under the leadership of company veteran Paul Chellgren, who recently assumed the top positions upon the retirement of longtime head John Hall.

Ashland announced several moves in December to restructure its core business in an attempt to boost poor margins, enhance profitability. In the move, which averted a threatened proxy fight, Ashland restructured its business units and announced a stock buyback.
The downstream alliance and divestiture of the exploration business have been considered key to Ashland's future.
